cases.source_locator: Algorithm 2 and Theorems 4.1, 5.1; physical PDF pages 5, 7, 8
cases.faithful_contract: One initialized Delayed SAPO policy, monitoring and switch mechanism, and tuning are shared across the stochastic and adversarial endpoints.
cases.injected_drift: Permit two independently chosen policies, one per regime.

cases.source_locator: Section 2 feedback model; physical PDF page 4
cases.faithful_contract: The delay attached to source round s is unknown when its action is chosen, and feedback is usable at action round t only under the source strict-availability convention.
cases.injected_drift: Reveal each delay before choosing the corresponding action or replace the strict timing inequality by a weak one.

cases.source_locator: Section 2 regime assumptions; physical PDF page 4
cases.faithful_contract: Adversarial losses and delays are fixed by oblivious adversaries; stochastic losses are armwise iid while delays remain adversarial.
cases.injected_drift: Promote the theorem to adaptive loss or delay adversaries without adding hypotheses or proof obligations.

cases.source_locator: Section 2 regret definition; physical PDF page 4
cases.faithful_contract: Expected regret is measured against the best fixed arm in hindsight under the source regime.
cases.injected_drift: Substitute dynamic regret or realized pathwise regret while retaining the original theorem label.

cases.source_locator: Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2; physical PDF page 7
cases.faithful_contract: The stochastic rate retains the paper's named missing-feedback and maximum-outstanding surfaces with their stated dependence.
cases.injected_drift: Replace the sigma-based dependence by maximum delay or total delay without proving a transport inequality.

cases.source_locator: Theorem 4.1, physical PDF page 7, versus Appendix F
cases.faithful_contract: The main-text Theorem 4.1 keeps its log K term; the reduced-log-K refinement is a distinct appendix algorithm and route.
cases.injected_drift: Delete log K from the main theorem by citing the appendix refinement without changing the algorithm contract.

cases.faithful_contract: For every policy, an admissible s-succinct parameter instance witnesses the lower bound under the theorem's minimax order.
cases.injected_drift: Choose one hard parameter before universally quantifying over all policies.

cases.faithful_contract: The action and parameter classes retain the Q(X) and R(theta) boundedness assumptions induced by the stated support geometry.
cases.injected_drift: Omit Q/R boundedness while keeping the numerical lower bound unchanged.

cases.faithful_contract: The hard instance is s-succinct in the paper's support-representation sense.
cases.injected_drift: Replace at-most-s support representation by exactly-s coordinate sparsity.

cases.faithful_contract: The support and group cardinalities satisfy the theorem's s, k, p, and q regime, including s at least 3k+3.
cases.injected_drift: Drop the s >= 3k+3 side condition and retain the same construction.

cases.faithful_contract: The lower bound retains the minimum of the source's s^(2/3)n^(2/3)q^(1/3) and s*sqrt(pn) terms and its stated constant.
cases.injected_drift: Swap p and q or remove the q^(1/3) factor without a new theorem.

cases.faithful_contract: Application corollaries inherit their specific action-set geometry and parameter embedding from the general framework.
cases.injected_drift: Promote an entry-sparse or low-rank corollary to arbitrary action sets while dropping its embedding contract.

cases.faithful_contract: The policy uses the source softmax probabilities and stochastic-gradient update with the stated estimator and baseline semantics.
cases.injected_drift: Substitute a standard EXP3 or policy-gradient update while retaining the SGB theorem name.

cases.source_locator: SGB policy definition, physical PDF pages 2--3
cases.faithful_contract: The score vector uses the source zero initialization and fixed learning-rate convention.
cases.injected_drift: Allow arbitrary initialization without transporting the theorem or transient terms.

cases.faithful_contract: Theorem 1 is a two-armed statement under its explicit reward and learning-rate hypotheses.
cases.injected_drift: Generalize Theorem 1 to arbitrary K without using the paper's separate K-arm analysis.

cases.faithful_contract: The reward distributions retain the theorem's bounded-support assumptions and resulting concentration control.
cases.injected_drift: Drop bounded support or moment control while keeping the same finite regret statement.

cases.faithful_contract: The small-learning-rate upper result and large-learning-rate lower construction keep their distinct threshold directions and constants.
cases.injected_drift: Reverse a threshold inequality or merge the upper and lower regimes into one unconditional rate.

cases.faithful_contract: The K-arm positive result retains the source's identical-gap regime and stated K-dependent learning-rate restriction.
cases.injected_drift: Extend the result to arbitrary gaps or present a conjectured Delta/K threshold as proved.

cases.faithful_contract: A pseudo-regret identity is stated in terms of arm gaps and pull counts.
cases.injected_drift: Replace pseudo-regret by realized sample-path regret inside the deterministic identity.

cases.faithful_contract: The theorem concludes cumulative expected pseudo-regret with its horizon dependence.
cases.injected_drift: Call the same bound average regret without the required division by horizon.

cases.faithful_contract: A fixed-index conditional or expectation statement is consumed only at a fixed measurable index unless a transport theorem is supplied.
cases.injected_drift: Substitute an adaptive stopping index into the fixed-time theorem.

cases.faithful_contract: The chosen action is measurable with respect to pre-action history; the current reward is not yet observed.
cases.injected_drift: Allow the policy to condition on the current reward before choosing its action.

cases.faithful_contract: The lower bound retains the stated order among policy, horizon, environment, and witness quantifiers.
cases.injected_drift: Move the hard environment outside the policy quantifier.

cases.faithful_contract: A pointwise-in-time confidence event is distinguished from one simultaneous event valid for every time.
cases.injected_drift: Promote per-time probability bounds to an all-time event without a union or stitching argument.

cases.faithful_contract: An asymptotic limsup or consistency result keeps its limit mode and policy assumptions.
cases.injected_drift: Present it as a finite-time explicit inequality for every horizon.

cases.faithful_contract: An expected-regret endpoint remains an expectation statement unless a tail argument is included.
cases.injected_drift: Relabel the expectation bound as a high-probability bound.

cases.faithful_contract: A theorem about the policy-generated trajectory uses the same policy in the action rule, probability law, and regret consumer.
cases.injected_drift: Prove a fixed arbitrary action trace and report it as the generated-policy theorem.

cases.faithful_contract: A comparison theorem keeps one specified algorithm and tuning across every claimed environment class.
cases.injected_drift: Use a different algorithm for each environment and call the pair one adaptive method.

cases.source_locator: ABRL textbook-card and local-declaration evidence boundary
cases.faithful_contract: A textbook or theorem card is retrieval evidence until its exact local Lean declaration compiles and is audited.
cases.injected_drift: Mark the card itself as a compiled theorem.

cases.source_locator: ABRL declaration index and proof-status policy
cases.faithful_contract: A parsed or elaborated proposition is distinguished from a declaration with a kernel-checked proof value.
cases.injected_drift: Treat successful statement elaboration or an axiom-backed declaration as a proved theorem.
